terms.gloss: crust: the hard outer layer of bread, a pie, or ice
evidence: Verg. G. 3.360: concrēscunt subitae currentī in flūmine crustae
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “the hard surface of a body, the rind, shell, crust”: of bread (Pliny), of ice on a river (Vergil), of a scab (Celsus). So the crust of a loaf, crusta pānis, and the crust of a pie or tart; the lexicon also lists it under “layer”. Of the pastry itself, the sheets of dough, Cato says tracta; of the base, solum (see “base”, of a cake or tart).

evidence: Cato Agr. 76: tracta singula in tōtum solum prīmum pōnitō
terms.comment: Lewis & Short (s.v. trahō): “a long piece of dough pulled out in making pastry”. Cato builds his placenta of such sheets, spread with cheese and honey.

phrases.latin: Crusta bene cocta est; jam exime.
phrases.english: The crust is nicely done; take it out now.
I don’t want the crust; you have it.
